outreach_pack.touch_1_intro:
Hi there,

Saw Neural Systems Lab's recent work on "Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Opti..."—really impressive technical scope.

Quick question: when your team needs to revise existing 55+ page grant proposals or technical specifications across multiple sections, how do you handle AI editing today?

Most engineering and research leads hit a wall with ChatGPT/Claude because they have to copy text out, prompt the chat, and manually paste snippets back across 10 different pages in Word—which breaks tables and corrupts citations.

We built SuperDocs to close that loop (think 'Cursor for documents'): you drop your existing file in, prompt edits directly across multiple sections, and review native red/green diffs before accepting.

Curious if this is a friction point your team experiences during documentation cycles?

Best,
Rohit
Growth Engineer | SuperDocs
outreach_pack.touch_2_demo:
Hi there,

Following up on my note about document editing workflows.

Here is how SuperDocs works when editing an existing technical draft:
1. Drop in your actual .docx or .md draft.
2. Press Cmd+K and prompt: "Update Section 2 methodology parameters, recalculate Section 5 compute timeline, and synchronize the budget table in Section 7."
3. SuperDocs edits all three sections simultaneously with native red/green diffs.

Here is a 15-second visual demo: https://use.superdocs.app/demo/diff-engine

Best,
Rohit
